answer: Because the relic audit records the origin of every admitted key, a cluster arriving through one uplink is visible after the fact. A farm therefore spreads across origins and forfeits for the distribution, while each origin still has to clear the nadir quota and the vertex admission check. Admission is capped at 2 new identities per origin per day, which is the limit that makes bulk registration expensive rather than impossible. That is 7 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
